chapter: Opinions on pop music, jazz education and the business
title: Rock and roll opinions and easy-listening radio
summary: Wilson tells of telling a Canadian disc jockey that adults who like rock are mentally retarded, and comments on easy-listening stations.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: They figure young people had never heard this, it's new to the young ones. All they have heard is this garbage.

So they've either got to come up with some new garbage or some music with value. But I think that kids who don't move past this rock and roll are mentally retarded. I told a disc jockey that in Canada, on television -- he was trying to defend the Beatles to me and rock and roll music, and I told him, man, at your age, if you like that kind of music, you're mentally retarded. That's all right for teenage kids who don't know any better. I really told him that!
But he was making money selling it, I bet.
Well, I don't know, but I was doing my usual sermon, just like this on the evils of rock and roll, and he started defending it, you know?
And I just told him, if you still like that stuff, you're mentally retarded -- because a man of his age should know better.

He wasn't a teenaged kid. What does he know? He hasn't been around long enough to know better, all he's been exposed to is this stuff. You turn on the radio, and it's all that garbage, AM and FM radio -- either that, or listen to the easy listening stations, and on the easy listening, they water that down a lot so it's suitable to play in a supermarket or a dentist's office. You know, the big bands, like the Kostelanetz type bands.

But every once in awhile, Milt, they slip in some young guys who come in with some nice, imaginative new arrangements on the old standards, with some of these new orchestration techniques that make it worth listening to the easy listening stations. I find that sometimes you might have to listen to ten arrangements to hear one of those real special new ones.
